content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or shows strong downward momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in correcting downward trends; true prices often dip below forecast before rebounding.
- Forecast tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts, especially in early days of a new sentiment cycle.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds high prices longer than observed in true outcomes.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overweights recent highs and fails to adjust for upcoming volatility.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows tendency to overestimate mid-term price stability, especially when sentiment is flat or mildly bullish.
- Correction needed when sentiment turns negative within 5–7 days of forecast horizon — model often fails to anticipate sharp drops.
- Overshoots are more common in the first 10 days of forecast horizon, especially after positive sentiment peaks.
- Model underestimates price drops following strong positive sentiment peaks — true prices often fall faster than forecast.
